intent: Count a commit as checked only if its check is less than a day old.

edit.summary:
I've proposed four changes to the `authoring` domain. All four came back with 0 issues, and I haven't confirmed or deployed any of them.

- **`objects.Commit`:** I added an optional integer property, `checked_at`.
- **`actions.record_check`:** It now also sets `target.checked_at` to `now()` when the check result is recorded.
- **`actions.approve_commit`:** The `checks-pass` precondition now needs `checks_passed == true` and `now() - checked_at < 86400`, which is under a day. The wording-only exception is unchanged, and so is `not-approved`. I reworded the reason to say the commit must have passed less than a day ago.

I left the `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` invariant and the `record_approval` precondition alone. The invariant is checked all the time, so a time limit would make it fail on commits that were valid when approved. The `record_approval` precondition still only requires a passed check.

The request didn't say how to read the time. I assumed `now()` exists and returns epoch seconds, and that the property is an integer. The tool raised no issue on `now()`, but it's worth checking in review. I made no changes to the `delivery` domain.
